subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should disabled heartbeat delivery preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable skip contract and add a separate human-readable hint/display, or should the machine reason be renamed?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but this changes exposed diagnostics for a default configuration path, and repository policy treats config/default diagnostic surfaces as compatibility-sensitive when operators may parse them.

options.title: Add additive hint/display
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add disabled-delivery explanatory text or a companion field, and update CLI/status formatting plus focused tests.

options.title: Rename the machine reason
options.body: Change the exposed reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting parser compatibility risk for any operator tooling that reads the current reason.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep relying on docs and accept the current low-priority operator confusion around `target-none`.

recommendation.title: Add additive hint/display
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add disabled-delivery explanatory text or a companion field, and update CLI/status formatting plus focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the default-target-none behavior and documented its migration tradeoff, so they have the strongest product context for the diagnostic contract.
